zh: 新唯物主义的慰藉
en: The consolation of new materialism

zh: 凯斯顿·萨瑟兰
en: KESTON SUTHERLAND

zh: 新唯物主义对资本主义表示厌恶时那种阴郁的半心半意，塑造并渲染了它关于生命未来的一切声明。资本主义被含糊地、顺带地、仿佛例行尽职般地责备，罪名是一连串古怪抽象的破坏行为：从用它的“公理”压扁“社会与文化运动”的“多向敞开”和“多种由好奇心驱动的知识实践”，到阻止“宇宙的虚拟性”继续作为“一切生命的共有形式”。
资本主义显然是这些劝诫的目标，因为它被点名；而资本主义干出这些事确实不可取；若不在新唯物主义无畏地宣告新的抵抗时与它携起手来，似乎有点闹别扭。这必定是抵抗，因为这个词也是一个关键词。任何一个诚实的资本主义憎恨者，为何会退缩，不敢“把‘活物质’当作一个以
）—地球为中心的过程，它以复杂方式与技术—社会、心理和自然环境互动，并抵抗资本主义利润原则（及其带来的结构性不平等）的过编码”，也不敢通过对抗而“最终落在一个横贯主体性的肯定性构成平面上”？那么，“一种可能启发、配合或支撑信息与科学实践，并抵抗发达资本主义对生命的跨物种商品化的后人类思想”，究竟能有什么害处？
抵抗当然受欢迎，无论它来自何种复杂互动过程或支撑性思想。即便它不能恰好来自人类，它仍可惠及（某些）人类。“人内部的非人，作为抵抗，是使（某些）人得以改变其生存条件、去制造、创造、发明的创造性力量。”
（这个括号将被理解为非常高效地表示：承认人类的多样性，以及他们相对于人内部的非人所处的显然极不相同的立场；同时表示谦逊，承认并非所有人类都能同样地通过重新使用这种创造性力量来改变其生存条件。）
en: The dismal half-heartedness of new materialism’s professions of antipathy to capitalism shapes and colours all its pronouncements on the future of life. Capitalism is reproved, indistinctly and in passing, as if with due diligence, for a catalogue of oddly abstract vandalisms: everything from squashing with its ‘axioms’ the ‘multi-directional opening out’ of ‘social and cultural movements’ and ‘multiple curiosity-driven knowledge practices’ to preventing the ‘virtuality of the cosmos’ from remaining ‘as a form of commons for all life’.

Capitalism evidently is the target of these remonstrances because it is called out by name, and these certainly are undesirable things for capitalism to get up to, and it may seem a bit sulky not to link arms with new materialism in its dauntless proclamations of the new resistance. Resistance it must be, because this word, too, is a keyword. Why would any honest hater of capitalism shrink from ‘taking “living matter” as a

-geo-centred process that interacts in complex ways with the techno-social, psychic and natural environments and resists the over-coding by the capitalist profit principle (and the structural inequalities it entails)’ and by opposing ‘end up on an affirmative plane of composition of transversal subjectivities’? What could possibly be the harm in ‘a posthuman thought that might inspire, work with or subtend informational and scientific practices and resist the trans-species commodification of life by advanced capitalism’?

Resistance, surely, is welcome, whatever process of complex interaction or subtensive thought it comes from. If it cannot exactly come from humans, it can still be of benefit to (some of) them. ‘The inhuman within the human, as resistance, is the creative force that enables (some) humans to transform their conditions of existence, to make, create, invent.’

(The parenthesis will be understood to signify, very efficiently, acknowledgement of the diversity of humans and the obviously very different positions they are in relative to the inhuman within the human, and humility with respect to the fact that not all humans will be equally enabled to transform their conditions of existence by making new use of this creative force.)

zh: 那种绝不能来自人类的抵抗，最终或许由物质本身提供——按新的方式理解，遵循德里达对“物质之去实体化”的解释，这种去实体化“源于把物质性铭写为与他者的不可能关系这一解构性铭写”；物质不再是物质，而是不可能的“物质性之力”。在这种新意义上，物质甚至还可以代表一种彻底回避人类的最精巧方法，这反过来会使抵抗从政治中解放出来。“作为对主体力量的瓦解，物质性之力不能通向任何政治纲领。”作为不能通向政治纲领的抵抗，物质性之力也把资本主义的对手——其作为主体的力量最终被彻底瓦解——从可被预期的未来的死胡同中解放出来。“因为物质性把我们引向彻底的他者，它也是不可预见之未来的开启，一个不能被预期为某种在场形式的
（将来）。”通过诉诸彻底他者、或诉诸“比具体实际更物质、更真实得令人诧异”的“不可能者”而来的抵抗，不允许其更激进的瓦解有任何例外，无论历史如何；最革命的批判，甚至革命战争，也与任何其他“基于理性计算或理想目的之筹划的目的性行动或目标导向行动”无异，因为那不可能的、比具体实际更真实的物质性之力，连同“任何目的论，例如马克思主义的目的论”，一起“抵抗并挫败”这一切。
en: Resistance that must not come from humans may ultimately be provided by matter itself, understood in the new way, following Derrida’s explanation of ‘the desubstantialization of matter that occurs as a result of the deconstructive inscription of materiality as the impossible relation to the other’, no longer as matter, but now as ‘the force of materiality’ that is impossible. Matter in this new sense may even in addition represent the most sophisticated method of avoiding the human altogether, which would in turn liberate resistance from politics. ‘As the undoing of the power of the subject, the force of materiality cannot lead to a political program.’ The force of materiality as resistance that cannot lead to a political program also frees the opponent of capitalism, whose power as a subject has at last been altogether undone, from the dead end of a future that can be anticipated. ‘Because it refers us to the radically other, materiality is also the opening of an unforeseeable future, an

(to come) that cannot be anticipated as a form of presence.’ Resistance by referral to the radically other, or ‘the impossible’ that ‘is curiously more material and real than concrete actuality’, can allow no exceptions to its more radical undoing, irrespective of history; the most revolutionary critique and even revolutionary warfare is no different from any other ‘purposive or end-oriented action that is based on rational calculations or the projection of an ideal end’, since the force of materiality that is impossible and more real than concrete actuality ‘resists and confounds’ all this along with ‘any teleology such as that of Marxism’.

zh: 用 Pheng Cheah 的话说，对新唯物主义而言，对资本主义的抵抗与对马克思主义的抵抗“令人诧异地”相似，甚至完全相同；从前者跳到后者，短得令人诧异。马克思主义一旦以新方式、以物质性之力、非人和横贯主体性的名义被成功抵抗，就显露出真面目：它并不是其死硬追随者至今仍执迷不悟地误认的那种资本主义革命批判，而是与资本主义一样，是一种病态的先驱，预示着将要到来的后人类内在性平面的活力——那个少数主义天堂，充满“从资本主义公理中解放出来的市场经济中各种新型经济生产实践”的繁荣。
美妙之处在于，抵达那里竟如此简单。进入它，就像进入克雷格·雷恩诗中的尘世天堂一样容易——别人只是把洗好的衣服从后花园收进来。我们只需放弃我们的“普罗米修斯式的人类统治自然观念”和马克思主义，同时放弃那由有毒律令所定义的“物种自恋”——该律令说“‘生命’必须保持特殊，也就是从根本上不同于物质”。
唯物主义仍然是——或者说，现在才第一次成为——这种转变的恰当载体，前提是首先根据一种“范式转换”迅速重估“马克思主义的遗产及其对唯物主义的特殊主张”：从（历史悠久且仍占主导的）把唯物主义与经济主义混为一谈，转向一种主要被定义为意指和过程中的主体性的革新版唯物主义。
en: The resistance of capitalism and the resistance of Marxism are, to use Cheah’s word, ‘curiously’ alike, or even identical, for new materialism, and it is a curiously short hop from one to the other. Marxism, once it has been successfully resisted, in the new way, in the name of the force of materiality, the inhuman and transversal subjectivities, turns out to be not the revolutionary critique of capitalism that its diehard adherents even now persist in mistaking it for, but, like capitalism, a morbid precursor to the vitality of the posthuman plane of immanence to come, that minoritarian paradise full of the flourishing of ‘new kinds of economically productive practices in a market economy liberated from capitalist axioms’.

And the beautiful thing is, what a simple thing it is to get there. It is as easy to enter as the heaven on earth accessed by somebody else bringing the washing in from the back garden in a Craig Raine poem. We need only give up our ‘Promethean ideas of human mastery over nature’ and Marxism, along with the ‘kind of species-narcissism’ defined by the toxic imperative that ‘“life” must remain special – that is, radically other to matter’.

Materialism is still, or, rather, is now for the first time, the proper vehicle for this transformation, provided that ‘the legacy of Marxism and its particular claim to materialism’ is first swiftly revaluated in the light of the ‘paradigm shift from the (time-honoured and still prevalent) conflation of materialism with economism to a revamped materialism defined primarily as signification and subjectivity-in-process.’

zh: 在马克思、恩格斯、狄慈根、普列汉诺夫、列宁、卢森堡和其他革命者使用该词的意义上，唯物主义从来不只是关于物质或物质性的理论，而始终也是、并且首先是革命教育学。

它是那些献身于摧毁资本的个体群体训练其“思维力”、并相互教导世界知识的途径。这种教导大多发生在学习机构之外，或逆着其文化进行，与学术资本和学术生涯的生产律令几乎没有关系。（这样一种想法：这种革命唯物主义有朝一日会因对主体性过于浪漫、因执迷于过时的人类、因轻信到竟试图详细预想未来社会关系的各种形式并在实践中加以实现——而不是退后一步、张口凝视“不可预见者的开启”——而被辞退或归档；以及这样一种想法：与那逆着学术资本而繁荣的旧式粗糙革命唯物主义相比，这个新未来的思想家们会在“新学术领域的蓬勃增长”中找到这种新的、改良版唯物主义的活力证据，这些领域“集中在若干富有创造性的跨学科枢纽，并已产生自己的超学科后代”

——对于“社会主义人道主义”黑暗中的旧辩证摸索者来说，这种想法恰恰会是可预见之物的定义：那就是他们早已熟悉的学院。）约瑟夫·狄慈根——这位自学成才的“哲学工人”、制革匠，也是马克思朋友与同代人中最专注的革命唯物主义阐释者——在写到“我们这些辩证的或社会民主主义的唯物主义者”时，他指的是，他的同志们也理解他指的是：我们这些资本主义社会与资产阶级思想的不共戴天的敌人，我们研究自然和世界的一切细节，是为了学会如何摧毁资本主义社会。
en: Materialism, in the sense in which Marx, Engels, Dietzgen, Plekhanov, Lenin, Luxemburg and other revolutionaries used the word, was never merely a theory of matter or materiality, but always also, and primarily, a revolutionary pedagogy.

It was how groups of individuals who dedicated their lives to the destruction of capital disciplined their ‘thought-capacity’ and taught themselves and each other about the world. Most of this teaching went on outside institutions of learning, or in defiance of their culture, and had little or nothing to do with the production imperatives of academic capital and the academic career. (The thought that this revolutionary materialism would one day be pensioned off or archived for being too romantic about subjectivity, for clinging to the outmoded human, and for being credulous enough to try to anticipate in detail and work out in practice forms of future social relations, instead of standing back and gaping at ‘the opening of the unforeseeable’; and the thought that, in preference to the old, crude revolutionary materialism that flourished in defiance of academic capital, the thinkers of this new future would find proof of the vitality of the new and improved materialism in ‘the exuberant growth’ of ‘new fields of scholarship … concentrated in a number of creative trans-disciplinary hubs, which have generated their own extra-disciplinary offspring’

– for the old dialectical gropers in the dark of ‘socialist humanism’, this thought would have been the definition of the foreseeable: it was the academy they already knew.) When Joseph Dietzgen, the self-taught ‘philosophical working man’, a tanner by trade, and the most dedicated exponent of revolutionary materialism among Marx’s friends and contemporaries, wrote of ‘us dialectical or Social-Democratic materialists’, he meant, and was understood by his comrades to mean, those of us who are the implacable enemies of capitalist society and bourgeois thought, who study nature and the world in all its detail in order to learn how to destroy capitalist society.

zh: 按照狄慈根，唯物主义革命教育学的第一条根本教训是：意识——包括诸如“物质之去实体化源于把物质性铭写为与他者的不可能关系这一解构性铭写”这样稀有的意识例子——应当“从谋生方式和途径”来解释。或者，如狄慈根更展开地所说：“人……获取每日面包的方式，一代人身体上
所处的文明水平，决定其思想立场，决定它构想——并且必须如何构想——真、善与正义、上帝、自由与不朽、哲学、政治与法律的方式。”

这一根本知识或许是教条式的，但不能通过任何临时的理论调和来达到。它只能在生活中践行。只有对于全心全意接受它并将其彻底内化的坚定革命者，它才是真实的、有意义的；到那时，它不再仅仅是一个命题，而是一个“批判性地牢固、不容置疑的立场”。（狄慈根解释说，正是他对1848年革命的经验，唤醒了他一种巨大的“获得批判性地牢固、不容置疑的立场的渴望”：唯物主义教育学观念的核心，是某种原初的攫取或俘获——生命被一种独特强度的欲望所攫取或俘获；这种强度经验，只有通过生活在一个真正革命可能性的时刻之中、并穿越这个时刻，才能被引爆。）
一旦这一知识成为牢固的立场，它便使其余一切变得可理解。但它并不以那种跨越世界的普罗米修斯式智性（或其新唯物主义漫画像）理解一切的方式去理解任何事物。它不导向全能的人类掌控，也不是其产物；事实上，它几乎恰恰相反。
en: The first and fundamental lesson of the revolutionary pedagogy of materialism, according to Dietzgen, is that consciousness – not excluding such rare examples of consciousness as the thought that ‘the desubstantialization of matter occurs as a result of the deconstructive inscription of materiality as the impossible relation to the other’ – is to be explained ‘from the way and manner of bread-winning’. Or, as Dietzgen more expansively put it, ‘that the way … in which man earns his daily bread, that the level of civilization on which a generation physically
, determines the mental standpoint or the way in which it conceives and must conceive the True, the Good and Right, God, Freedom and Immortality, Philosophy, Politics and Law.’

This fundamental knowledge, which may indeed be dogmatic, cannot be reached by any temporary theoretical accommodation. It can only be lived. It is true and it makes sense only for the determined revolutionary who accepts it wholeheartedly and radically internalizes it; it is then no longer merely a proposition, but a ‘critically firm, undoubted standpoint’. (Dietzgen explains that it was his experience of the revolutions of 1848 that awoke in him a great ‘desire to acquire a critically firm, undoubted standpoint’: essential to the idea of materialist pedagogy is some kind of originary seizure or captivation of life by a singular pitch of desire, an experience of intensity that can only be made to erupt by living in and through a moment of real revolutionary possibility).

Once this knowledge is a firm standpoint, it makes sense of everything else. But it does not make sense of anything in the way that a Promethean intellect astride the world (or its new materialist caricature) would make sense of everything. It does not lead to and is not the product of an omnipotent human mastery; in fact, it is almost the very opposite.

zh: 狄慈根的革命唯物主义植根于一种持久的惊奇：一切可以被思考、考察、学习、理解、领会或尝试的事物都是无穷无尽的。这是一种革命教育学：学习这项工作的力量在于这样一个现实——这项工作永远不会完成；不是因为人类智力太少或太不安分，而是因为“被给予我们的思维力作为材料的东西，与空间一样无限”。
这对每个对象、每个生命、每个观念、每种可能性都成立：没有任何事物会被思想穷尽，即便它就在眼前或可以预见；思想总能做更多，总能发现更多，总能感知和认识更多。狄慈根写道：“无论一个人想测量无限，还是只想测量最小的原子，他总得面对不可测量者。自然，无论作为整体还是其部分，都是不可穷尽的，不能认识至其最后一个粒子——因而没有开端和终结。”
这是一种“社会民主主义”的无限：其重点完全落在对象的不可穷尽性上，因此也落在发现的劳动上——任何真正尝试的人，只要认真接触任何对象，就会进入这种无尽地引人入胜、无尽地令人沮丧、也无尽地给予回报的发现劳动。
en: Dietzgen’s revolutionary materialism is rooted in permanent wonder at the inexhaustibleness of everything that can be thought, examined, learned, understood, picked up or tried out. It is a revolutionary pedagogy for which the power of the work of learning consists in the reality that this work is never done, not because the human intellect is too little or too restless, but because ‘the stuff that is given as material for our thought-capacity is as infinite as space’.

This is true of every object, every life, every idea, every possibility: nothing is ever exhausted by thought, not even when it is present or foreseeable, but there is always more that thought can do, always more to find, always more to sense and to know. ‘Whether one wants to measure the Infinite or merely the smallest atom, one always has to deal with the Immeasurable’, Dietzgen wrote. ‘Nature, both as a whole and in its parts, is inexhaustible, not knowable to its last particle – consequently without beginning and end.’

This is a ‘social democratic’ type of infinity: its emphasis falls squarely on the inexhaustibleness of the object and the therefore endlessly compelling, endlessly frustrating, endlessly rewarding work of discovery that follows serious engagement with any object at all, by anyone at all who really tries.

zh: 智性——或者用狄慈根那种咄咄逼人的直接唯物主义语言来说，“头脑”——在唯物主义动机的驱动下，对这无限材料所做的是工作。“思想就是工作。”
重新概念化工作的革命唯物主义决心，对马克思主义女性主义批判和当代社会再生产理论始终具有根本意义。正如南希·哈索克所写：
en: What the intellect – or in Dietzgen’s aggressively direct materialist language, what the ‘head’ – does with this infinite stuff, when activated by materialist motives, is work. ‘Thought is work.’
The revolutionary materialist determination to reconceptualize work has remained fundamental for Marxist feminist critique and for contemporary social reproduction theory. As Nancy Hartsock wrote:

zh: 女性的解放——以及一切人类的解放——取决于理解工作对我们作为个体的发展至关重要，取决于在我们的生活中为我们的工作创造新的位置。我们必须发展出一种关于工作本身的新概念。为开始这一过程，我们必须弄清楚资本主义与父权制的工作组织究竟哪里出了问题，并界定
工作的要求。
en: The liberation of women – and all human beings – depends  on understanding that work is essential to our development as  individuals and on creating new places in our lives for our work. We  must develop a new conception of work itself. To begin this process,  we must clarify what is wrong with the capitalist and patriarchal  organization of work and define the requirements of
work.

zh: “人类”在此显然不是指“非动物”或“非机器”，而是指“资本主义与父权制一直阻止我们为自己共同去做的事”。
在这个意义上，人类工作很可能是动物或机器也能做的工作（关键在于，我们必须通过斗争去发现）。唯物主义动机是整个身体的动机，而不仅是头脑的动机。无产阶级哲学家狄慈根坚持说：“思维是身体的工作。”
感官经验是一种思想，而思想是一种感官经验。许多新唯物主义者的批评中有一个古怪观念，认为“现代西方文化中主导性的物质观念是：物质本质上是被动的东西”
；与这种观念相反，对狄慈根——他与恩格斯是马克思主义传统中最杰出的唯物主义阐释者——而言，物质就是一切，无处不在，既有主动也有被动，既存在于心灵最内在的活动，也存在于引力之中。
en: ‘Human’ evidently does not mean, here, ‘not animal’ or ‘not machine’, but ‘what we have been prevented from doing together, for ourselves, by capitalism and by patriarchy’.

Human work in this sense might very well be work that animals or machines could do: the point is, we have to fight to find out). Materialist motives are motives of the whole body, not only of the head. ‘Thinking is bodily work’, Dietzgen the proletarian philosopher insisted.

Sensory experience is a kind of thought, and thought is a sensory experience. Contrary to the curious idea, central to the criticism of many new materialists, that ‘the predominant sense of matter in modern Western culture has been that it is essentially passive stuff’,

for Dietzgen, who with Engels was the most prominent exponent of materialism in the Marxist tradition, matter is everything and everywhere, active and passive, in the most intimate activity of the mind as well as in the force of gravity.

zh: 我们现代社会主义者并不持有那种狭隘意见，认为有重量、可触知的物质才是

物质。我们认为花香、声音和气味也是物质的。我们不把力设想为物质的单纯附属物、单纯谓词，也不把可触知的物质设想为统治一切属性的“那个东西”。可以说，我们对物质和力的构想是民主的。一方与另一方具有同等价值；一切个别之物都只是整个自然整体的属性、附属物、谓词或特质。大脑不是斗牛士，心智功能也不是从属的仆役。不，我们现代唯物主义者主张，功能之为独立之物的程度，与可触知的大脑团块或任何其他物质性完全相同（都同样多，也同样少）。思想，连同其起源和本性，也是与任何其他事物一样真实的事物和材料，值得研究。
en: We, modern Socialists, are not of the narrow opinion that the  ponderable and tangible matter is matter

. We hold  that the scent of flowers, sounds and smells are also material. We  do not conceive the forces as mere appendices, mere predicates of  matter, and matter, the tangible one as ‘the thing’ which dominates  over all properties. Our conception of matter and force is, so to  speak, democratic. One is of the same value as the other; everything  individual is but the property, appendix, predicate or attribute of  the entire Nature as a whole. The brain is not the matador and  the mental functions are not the subordinate servants. No, we  modern materialists assert that the function is as much and as  little an independent thing as the tangible brain-mass or any other  materiality. The thoughts, too, their origin and nature, are just as  real matters and materials worthy of study as any.

zh: 狄慈根对无限自然的不可穷尽性、对每个对象之于头脑和感官的无限性的唯物主义惊奇，以及他对那种幼稚而幻想的观念的蔑视——这种观念把人或人类设想为一个普罗米修斯式的项目经理，蹲踞在宇宙之上并统治一切——在数十年间一直是马克思主义传统中革命唯物主义特性的根本。“外部世界、客观世界不仅存在于我之外，也存在于我之内，在我自己的皮肤之内”，格奥尔基·普列汉诺夫写道——他是1917年革命前俄国最有影响的马克思革命唯物主义倡导者。“人只是自然的一部分，是存在的一部分；因此，他的思想与他的存在之间不可能有矛盾。”
对普列汉诺夫和狄慈根来说，如果没有一种植根于惊奇的工作理论，就不可能有有意义的唯物主义，换言之，也不可能有给决心摧毁资本主义社会的革命者的教育学；这种惊奇面对的是：一切尚待学习、理解、认识、并因而最终为工人实现或

为现实之物的不可穷尽性——在此之前，工人在资本之下注定以被压碎、被掏空的间接或直接奴役状态存在。没有工作理论，就不可能有革命唯物主义。狄慈根的工作理论既涉及我们现在所做的工作——已经作为“思想”和“谋生”完成的工作——也涉及尚未完成、却仍可能完成的工作：如果我们从资本主义生产关系中解放出来，并献身于探索自然、思想本身、与我们共同工作的他人，以及任何认真吸引我们注意的对象的无限性。现在必须进行思想工作，以构想这些新的、未来的工作形式和对不可穷尽者的探索；也正是通过这种思想工作，资本之下存在的绝对贫困才能越来越令人难以忍受地得到明确揭示。狄慈根写道，唯物主义必须学会“不可知者如何转变为可知者”

；对一个唯物主义者来说，这一点尤其适用于两种情况。唯物主义者必须研究：资本主义对生命的碾压给工人造成的苦难——这种苦难当然被感受和忍受，但就其真相而言可能仍“不可知”——如何能够被清楚而牢固地认识。唯物主义者还必须研究：在摧毁资本之后可能赢得的世界和可能过上的生活，如何能尽可能完整地保持在可达范围内：作为愿景、作为诗、作为幻想、作为科学、作为预测、作为目的论、作为欲望、作为一个纲领或一个梦；无论如何都要全心全意，并且始终处在不可预见的未来——或尚不能被绘制成社会蓝图之物——与可知的未来——或被压碎的人们确实知道自己首先想要、甚至愿冒生命危险去争取之物——之间最鲜明的张力与重叠点上。这些想法很简单，甚至粗糙，在哲学上是原始的：思想是工作，思想是身体劳动，意识由谋生方式决定，世界对思想而言不可穷尽，我们永远达不到终点，总还有一切有待学习和争取。它们简单，一是不需要非常复杂的逻辑，二是它们不考虑大量复杂性和偶然性，几乎到了让人难以相信偶然性真的被考虑过的地步。作为革命唯物主义教育学的教训，它们不难理解。它们容易理解，却极难与之共处。
en: Dietzgen’s materialist wonder at the inexhaustibleness of infinite nature and the infinity of every object for the head and the senses remained fundamental to the character of revolutionary materialism in the Marxist tradition for many decades, as did his contempt for the infantile and fantastical idea of man or the human as a Promethean project manager squatting on the cosmos and dominating everything. ‘The outer world, the objective world, does not exist only outside me, but also within me, inside my own skin’, wrote Georgy Plekhanov, the most influential proponent of Marx’s revolutionary materialism in Russia before the revolution of 1917. ‘Man is only a part of nature, a part of being; that is why there can be no contradiction between his thought and his being.’

For Plekhanov, as for Dietzgen, there can be no meaningful materialism, or, in other words, no pedagogy for revolutionaries determined to destroy capitalist society, without a theory of work rooted in wonder at the inexhaustibleness of everything that remains to be learned, understood, known, and, consequently and ultimately, realized or

as reality for workers who, until that time, are condemned under capital to exist in crushed and voided states of indirect or direct slavery. There can be no revolutionary materialism that is not a theory of work. Dietzgen’s theory of work is about both the work that we do now, work that is done already as ‘thought’ and as ‘breadwinning’, and work that is not done yet, but that might yet be done, if and when we free ourselves from capitalist relations of production, and dedicate our lives to exploring the infinity of nature, of thought itself, of others who work with us, and of every object that seriously engages our attention. The work of thought that is necessary now to conceive these new, future forms of work and exploration of the inexhaustible is also how the absolute poverty of existence under capital can be made more and more excruciatingly explicit. Materialism must learn ‘how the unknowable changes into the knowable’, Dietzgen wrote;

and for a materialist this is true in two cases above all. The materialist must study how the suffering inflicted on the worker by the capitalist crushing of life – suffering that is certainly felt and endured, but that may yet be ‘unknowable’ for what it is – can be clearly and firmly known. And the materialist must study how the world that may be won and the life that may be lived after the destruction of capital can be kept as fully as possible within reach: as vision, as poetry, as fantasy, as science, as prediction, as teleology, as desire, as a programme or as a dream; in any case wholeheartedly, and always at the most vivid point of tension and overlap between the unknowable future, or what cannot yet be drawn up as a blueprint for society, and the knowable future, or what people who are crushed do know that they want above all else and would even risk life to get. These are simple thoughts, rough even, and philosophically primitive: thought is work, thought is bodily labour, consciousness is determined by the manner of breadwinning, the world is inexhaustible for thought, we never get to the end, there is always everything still to learn and to win. They are simple thoughts in the sense that they do not require a very complex logic, and in the sense that they leave out of consideration a great number of complexities and contingencies, almost to the point where it is difficult to believe that contingency has really been reckoned with at all. As lessons of a revolutionary materialist pedagogy, they are not difficult to understand. They are easy to understand, but intensely difficult to live with.

Polystyrene, human being, exoplanet or bat shit, none of this need be brought down to the same level by a ‘flat ontology’, because everything is already equal. Capital takes care of that. Objects already ‘have a life of their own’, prior to the vivifications of new materialism: an indifferent life.
Everything is ‘some use-value’ for value ‘to exist in’, and it is ‘a matter of complete indifference what particular object serves this purpose’.

zh: 这就是关于“无差异”的真相，马克思通过对物质特定性之灭绝的诗性具体化，使这一真相发出回响。若不借助强烈而令人信服的诗性攻击，这样的真相无法像在《资本论》中那样发出回响。一方面因为其中没有攻击性，或者说没有令人信服的攻击性；另一方面因为它毫无诗意，新唯物主义关于一切物质平等的这一思想版本，最终让人感觉像是马克思所谓“乌托邦”那类华丽遐想的晚期开花。按照马克思，乌托邦思想的问题不在于它过于幻想，也不在于它设想了一个对现实而言太好或太完美的世界；问题在于它永远无法指明真正抵达它所设想的世界所必需的工作。它对如何抵达那里不感兴趣，因为它并不真正关心暴力：既不关心资本主义生产过程中不可阻挡的暴力形式——现在存在、必须被斗争和废除的暴力，也不关心那种将不可避免地成为寻找和建设我们所知自己想要的世界之必要与本质的革命暴力。理论方案足以用来设想一个只需在理论上被欲求的世界，也适合那些不必日复一日承受这种处境的人：被难以忍受地压碎，觉得自己的存在渺小如尘埃、令人无法忍耐，探索无限的一切可能性也都被切断和封闭。但对于确实那样被压碎、每天确实感受到这一切、且无路可走的人类来说，那些关于攻击与暴力的矜持审慎的理论化风格，或干脆完全回避攻击与暴力的理论，不仅可笑，而且猥亵。
en: This is the truth about ‘indifference’, the truth that Marx makes resound by a poetic specification of the extinction of material specificity. Truth like this could not be made to resound as it does in

without intense, compelling poetic aggression. Partly for the reason that there is no aggression in it, or none that is compelling, and partly for the reason that it is not remotely poetic, new materialism’s version of this thought about the equality of all matter ends up feeling like a late blossoming of the species of florid reverie that Marx called ‘utopian’. The problem with utopian thought, according to Marx, was not that it was too fantastical or that it envisioned a world too good or perfect for reality; the problem was that it never could specify the work that is actually necessary to get to the world it envisioned. It was not interested in how to get there, because it was not really interested in violence: neither in the forms of violence that are inexorable in the capitalist process of production, the violence that exists now and that must be fought and abolished, nor in the revolutionary violence that will unavoidably be necessary and essential to finding and building the world that we know we want. Theoretical solutions suffice for envisioning a world that need only be desired in theory, and are good for human beings who are not crushed right now, every day, unbearably, to the point where their existence feels unendurably speck-like, and for whom every possibility of exploration of the infinite is cut off and shut down. But for human beings who are crushed like that and do feel all those things, every day, and who have no way out, reticent and cautious styles of theorizing about aggression and violence, or theories that simply avoid aggression and violence altogether, are not only risible, but obscene.

zh: 新唯物主义者罗西·布拉伊多蒂写道：“对生命本身的关注，可能促成一种以生物为中心的平等主义，迫使人们从‘生命力量’的角度重新思考主体性概念。”这种促成平等主义、迫使重新思考主体性概念的关注，也
en: ‘The focus on life itself’, writes the new materialist Rosi Braidotti, ‘may encourage a sort of biocentred egalitarianism, forcing a reconsideration of the concept of subjectivity in terms of “life-forces.”’ This focus that encourages egalitarianism and forces reconsideration of the concept of subjectivity also

zh: 使自我与他者的关系发生错位，同时也重新定义这种关系：它把性别化、种族化和自然化的轴线从二元对立转向一种更复杂、较少对立性的互动模式。
en: dislocates but also redefines the relationship between self and  other by shifting the axes of genderization, racialization, and  naturalization away from a binary opposition into a more complex  and less oppositional mode of interaction.

zh: 这种对立性的互动模式，无论它可能是什么，都是新唯物主义表示异议时的常规靶子。戴安娜·库尔和萨曼莎·弗罗斯特在她们合编的文集《新唯物主义：本体论、能动性与政治》的导言中谨慎地说，新唯物主义思想家这一多样领域中的所有人共同感受到的一点，是“对对立性思维方式的厌恶”。

想来，对立的思维方式不能被简单地反对，但可以、而且经常在原则上被不优先选择，转而优先选择某种与“移动”事物有关的“更复杂”的东西。对立性思维本身复杂性较低这一点，已不再可供讨论。那种复杂思维的原始形式，始于承认对抗力量或不可调和差异的僵局——这种僵局不能被消解，必须被生活（尽可能充分地，无论需要多久，无论进展多慢），并最终被摧毁——如今被默默跳过。但正是这种思维方式——在旧意义上“对立”，因为它是至死方休的冲突——把18世纪的唯物主义转变为马克思名言中的“批判的武器”和一种革命教育学。对立——坚定的、不可调和的、绝对的——不仅是这一转变的条件，也是它的全部要点。对狄慈根而言，马克思和恩格斯的新唯物主义的要点恰恰在于：它是“社会民主主义的唯物主义”，是革命者手中的武器，用以对抗资产阶级国家和资本对生命的统治。社会民主主义的新唯物主义，与旧的“形而上学唯物主义”相反：后者只关心具体现象的本性，不关心心灵与物质的关系，因而不关心被理解为包含不可测量者的整个自然（革命唯物主义“在一个概念中既拥抱真实的幻想，也拥抱真实的铺路石”）。
en: The oppositional mode of interaction, whatever that might be, is the regular target of new materialist demurral. In their introduction to the volume of essays they co-edited,
, Diana Coole and Samantha Frost carefully say that one thing the diverse field of new materialist thinkers all feel in common is an ‘antipathy toward oppositional ways of thinking’.

Oppositional ways of thinking cannot, presumably, just be opposed, but can be and regularly are dispreferred in principle in favour of something ‘more complex’ to do with ‘shifting’ things. The lesser complexity of oppositional thinking itself is no longer up for discussion. The primitive forms of complex thinking that start with recognition of an impasse of opposed forces or irreconcilable differences that cannot be dissolved but must be lived (as fully as possible, for as long as it might take, however slow the progress) and ultimately destroyed are skipped over in silence. But it was this form of thinking, ‘oppositional’ in the old sense that it was a conflict to the death, that was responsible for transforming the materialism of the eighteenth century into a ‘weapon of critique’, in Marx’s famous phrase, and a revolutionary pedagogy. Opposition – steadfast, irreconcilable, absolute – was not merely the condition of this transformation, but also the whole point of it. For Dietzgen, the point of the new materialism of Marx and Engels was precisely that it is the ‘materialism of Social Democracy’, a weapon in the hands of revolutionaries opposed to the bourgeois state and the domination of life by capital. The new materialism of Social Democracy is the opposite of the old ‘metaphysical materialism’ that was concerned only with the nature of concrete phenomena and not with the relation of mind to matter and therefore not with the whole of nature understood as comprehending the immeasurable’ (revolutionary materialism ‘embraces in one conception both true fancies and true paving stones’).

zh: 无论一个人想测量无限，还是只想测量最小的原子，他总得面对不可测量者。自然，无论作为整体还是其部分，都是不可穷尽的，不能认识至其最后一个粒子——因而没有开端和终结。
en: Whether one wants to measure the Infinite or merely the smallest  atom, one always has to deal with the Immeasurable. Nature, both  as a whole and in its parts, is inexhaustible, not knowable to its last  particle – consequently without beginning and end.

zh: 这听起来像神秘主义，直到人们认清它实际上是什么：一种无产阶级的劝勉，号召把握全部经验，探索一切生命和世界，持续观看，始终把可设想的最高目标保持在视野中，永不放弃。不能把任何事物“认识至其最后一个粒子”这一不可能性，并不具有对思想施加立法性限制的性质：它不是对康德批判性地确立知识界限所作的比喻性简化。狄慈根这一本质上是劝勉性的原则，其要点在于它作为无产阶级手中的武器是有用的：一种击退压抑之痛苦、劈开智性瘫痪的手段。其哲学上的遮掩故事是黑格尔式的：拒绝接受唯心主义把现实以“自在之物”的形式放逐到知识和经验无法触及的领域。但对狄慈根而言，真正重要的强调在于这一断言：没有任何事物能在被穷尽的意义上被认识。
en: This sounds like mysticism, until it is recognized for what it really is: a proletarian exhortation, a call to seize hold of the whole of experience, to explore all of life and the world, to keep looking, to keep the greatest conceivable goals in sight, and never to give up. The impossibility of knowing anything ‘to its last particle’ does not have the character of a legislative restriction on thought: it is not a figurative simplification of Kant’s critical establishment of the limits of knowledge. The point of Dietzgen’s essentially exhortative principle is that it is useful as a weapon in the hands of the proletariat: a means of fighting off the agonies of inhibition and hacking clear of intellectual paralysis. The philosophical cover story is the Hegelian one about refusing to accept the idealist ejection of reality in the form of ‘thing in itself’ into a region beyond the reach of knowledge and experience. But the vital emphasis for Dietzgen is on the assertion that nothing can be known in the sense of being exhausted.

zh: 世界上没有任何事物，连一个原子也没有，能被彻底认识尽。世界上的一切事物在其秘密中都是不可穷尽的，正如它在其本质中是不朽而不可摧毁的。尽管如此，我们每天越来越多地学会认识事物，并认识到没有任何东西对我们的心灵是封闭的。
en: Nothing in the world, not an atom of it, is to be known out and out.  Everything in the world is inexhaustible in its secrets, no less than  it is imperishable and indestructible in its essence. With all that, we  learn every day more and more to know the things, and learn that  there is nothing which is closed to our mind.

zh: 对狄慈根来说，这是特定的革命唯物主义或“社会民主主义”唯物主义的理论基石。革命唯物主义不单纯是一种哲学学说或世界观，而是一种教育学：它是“我们［革命者］每天越来越多地学习……并认识到没有什么对我们的心灵封闭”的方式——同样，正因为如此，没有任何关系形式、任何工作形式对我们的生命封闭。革命唯物主义教育学不能没有“不可测量者”“无限”和“不可穷尽者”，不仅因为这种唯物主义必须与一个只允许（如蒲鲁东所说）“消费能力”无限的社会作斗争，更根本地因为“每天越来越多地”学习、从经验中学到一切可能的东西，才能使一个充满待发展潜能的人类主体的可能性保持活着——而资本系统地把它吸空抽干，掏成主体的一幅怪诞戏仿：劳动力。面对一个“不可穷尽的”世界——其任何部分都不对心灵“封闭”——的唯物主义者，与那种只作为一定量的社会必要“劳动力”而存在、等待被耗尽的工人相反；从价值对象性来看，工人在耗尽过程持续之前和之后都无足轻重。唯物主义教育学所激活的生命，与那种只不过是“生产过程的主观要素”的存在的怪诞空虚之间的对立，并不只是范畴的对立——不是各种新唯物主义者显然都觉得“反感”的“对立性思维方式”的产物——而是一场工人深切感受到的斗争，一种必须每天承受并正面回应的痛苦来源，甚至要“每天越来越多地”如此。
en: For Dietzgen, this was the theoretical bedrock of specifically revolutionary or ‘Social Democratic’ materialism. Revolutionary materialism is not a philosophical doctrine or world-view, simply, but a pedagogy: it is how ‘we [revolutionaries] learn every day more and more … and learn that there is nothing which is closed to our mind’ – just as, and for this very reason, there is no form of relation, no form of work, that is closed to our lives. Revolutionary materialist pedagogy cannot do without the ‘immeasurable’, the ‘infinite’ and the ‘inexhaustible’, not only because this materialism must fight against a society in which it is only (as Proudhon put it) ‘the power to consume’ that is allowed to be infinite, but more fundamentally because learning ‘every day more and more’, learning everything possible from experience, is what keeps alive the possibility of a human subject full of potential to be developed, the same subject that capital systematically sucks empty and hollows out into the grotesque parody of a subject, ‘labour-power’. The materialist who confronts an ‘inexhaustible’ world, no part of which is ‘closed’ to the mind, is the opposite of the worker who exists only as a quantity of socially necessary ‘labour-power’ to be exhausted, and who is, value-objectively speaking, of no consequence before or after the duration of the process of that exhaustion. This opposition of the life activated by materialist pedagogy to the grotesque emptiness of existence as nothing but ‘the subjective element in the production process’ is not a mere opposition of categories – a product of the ‘oppositional ways of thinking’ that new materialists of every sort apparently find ‘antipathetic’ – but a struggle that is deeply felt by the worker and a source of pain that must be lived with and lived up to, every day, and even ‘every day more and more’.

zh: 这种对立根本无法以“二元对立过时了”或“二元对立不够复杂”之类的说法打发。这是工人从根本上摆脱不掉的对立，是生命的一种基本规定。费尔巴哈曾激情地称之为“令人厌恶的矛盾”（
）的那种矛盾，内在于这种对立之中。
那种只不过是非人力量之耗尽的、作为戏仿形式的主体，是
：它是未被活过的生命的被感受到的事实。
这就是马克思在《资本论》中把商品形式描述为“可感觉而又超感觉的”这一表述的真相——这个表述人们早已熟悉，但即便现在也几乎未被理解，或只被小心翼翼地把握（这个谓词是马克思从黑格尔那里取来的，一如既往带有讽刺风格）。商品就是被感受到的未被活过的生命。
en: This opposition is simply not dismissible by talk of the outmodedness or insufficient complexity of binaries. It is an opposition that workers are fundamentally stuck with, a basic determination of life. Contradiction, of the kind passionately characterized by Feuerbach as ‘abhorrent contradiction’ (
), is intrinsic to this opposition.
The parody form of the subject that is nothing but the exhaustion of a nonhuman power is
: it is the felt fact of unlived life.
This is the truth of Marx’s long familiar but even now scarcely understood or only delicately grasped description of the commodity form in
as ‘sensuous-supersensuous’ (a predicate that Marx lifted from Hegel, as usual in satirical style). The commodity is felt unlived life.

zh: 一极是能够在发现他人、对象和世界真正不可穷尽性的工作中“每天越来越多地”实现的主体性；另一极是这种主体性被无差异地转化为劳动力的抹除与封堵——这种劳动力存在只是为了在价值增殖中被耗尽。这种极化就是马克思在《德意志意识形态》中所说的“每个单独无产者的个性与劳动、与强加于他的生活条件之间的矛盾”。

劳动，在这种特定的资本主义形式中作为“生活条件”，随着无产者被迫服从它的时间越长，就日益“在其无内容性中令人憎恨”，它在如下意义上矛盾：对无产者而言，它既是一切，又是虚无。劳动是无产者“终其一生”的全部，同时劳动又与无产者“分离”或在其“之外”，甚至在其触及范围之外；这不仅是因为他不能为自己决定它将是什么活动、他要做多久、在何处何时去做，而且——对马克思来说最重要的是——他无法越过其无内容性，用狄慈根所描述的那种发现之真理去填充它：狄慈根在革命唯物主义劝勉中号召一种从经验中学习的方式，以揭示世界真正的不可穷尽性。真正自由的工作形式恰恰会这样做，会成为“每天越来越多地”关于自我、他人、对象和世界的知识——即便它令人沮丧、痛苦或在其他方面没有产出。狄慈根用一个音乐类比让这种唯物主义观念变得可理解：
en: At one pole, a subjectivity that can be realized ‘every day more and more’ in the work of discovering the true inexhaustibleness of others, objects and the world; at the other pole, the blanking out and blocking in of that subjectivity by its indifferent conversion into labour-power that exists only in order to be exhausted in the valorization of value. This polarization is what, in
, Marx calls ‘the contradiction between the individuality of each separate proletarian and labour, the condition of life forced upon him’.

Labour, in this specifically capitalist form as a ‘condition of life’ that grows steadily more ‘hateful in its contentlessness’ the longer the proletarian is forced to submit to it, is contradictory in the sense that for the proletarian it is both everything and nothing. Labour is all that the proletarian is ‘for the entirety of his life’, and at the same time labour is ‘separate’ from or ‘outside’ of the proletarian and even out of his reach, not only in the sense that he cannot determine for himself what activity it will be, or how long he will do it for, or where and when he will do it, but also, and most importantly for Marx, that he cannot get past its contentlessness and fill it with the truth of discovery described by Dietzgen in his revolutionary materialist exhortation to a kind of learning from experience that discloses the true inexhaustibleness of the world. A form of work that is really free would do precisely that, and would be ‘every day more and more’ knowledge – of oneself, others, of objects, of the world – even when it is frustrating, painful or otherwise unproductive. Dietzgen makes sense of this idea of materialism with a musical analogy:

zh: 在我看来，只有彻底懂得如何演奏小提琴的人，才知道小提琴的本性——他知道其中有什么，也知道要做什么才能把它发挥出来。
en: In my opinion only that person is able to understand the nature of a  violin who knows thoroughly how to play it – who knows what there  is in it and what is to be done to bring it out of it.

zh: 正是在演奏小提琴数十年之后，指尖无穷小的运动的无限性才开始在现实中显现——也就是说，才真正被感受和认识——成为狄慈根所描述的那种“实质真理”。正是在这里，无穷小真正成为无限：感觉成为“通过眼睛、耳朵和手所构想”的真理，这种真理是“普遍生命的产物”。
在这个意义上，物质的人严格说来就像物质的小提琴：相互认识的要旨，是学会如何彻底认识彼此，发现我们自身之中有什么，以及要做什么才能把它从我们身上带出来；而革命唯物主义的要旨，是教会我们自己如何改造社会生产劳动，以便我们真的通过共同工作来认识自己和他人。那时，生产将是我们自己生命的生产。
en: It is after playing the violin for decades that the infinity of the infinitesimal movement of a fingertip begins to appear in reality – that is, really to be felt and known – as the sort of ‘substantial truth’ that Dietzgen describes. This is where the infinitesimal becomes infinite for real: sensation becomes truth ‘conceived through the eyes, ears and hands’ that is the ‘product of universal life’.

The material human being is in this sense strictly like the material violin: the point of knowing each other is to learn how to know each other thoroughly, to find out what there is in ourselves and what is to be done to bring it out of us, and the point of revolutionary materialism is to teach ourselves how to transform socially productive work so that we really do learn about ourselves and others by working together. Production will then be the production of our own lives.

zh: 工作是无限的，因为个体不可穷尽。新唯物主义或后人类把马克思主义漫画化为一种统治自然的哲学，未能认出这种关于工作与不可穷尽者之根本关系的愿景，也错过了它的诗性特征。这并不令人惊讶，因为新唯物主义对工作无话可说。
en: The work is infinite because individuals are inexhaustible. The new materialist or post-human caricature of Marxism as a philosophy of domination over nature fails to recognize this vision of a fundamental relation of work to the inexhaustible, and misses its poetic character. This is not surprising, because new materialism has nothing to say about work.

zh: 只有一种被周密保护起来、拒不承认这场斗争之现实（它在今天、对如今活着的绝大多数人而言的现实）的理论，才会把这种关于唯物主义教育学揭示不可穷尽者之力量革命乐观主义，重新解释为一种过时的幻想：一个掌控性的、普罗米修斯式的人类跨立在自然之上，试图统治或殖民一切。狄慈根和马克思试图概念化的关系——以无产阶级的名义、为个体工人而做的，诗性的、充满激情的、具有哲学胆识的概念化——不是全知全能的人类主体与一个只为被统治或殖民而存在的自然之间的关系；这种关系是工作与不可穷尽者之间的关系。如果说某种掌控对于实现这种关系而可能从事的工作仍然不可或缺，那是因为正是在发现的远端，这种意义上的工作往往变得最为艰苦、最为引人入胜、要求最高、最为紧张。
en: Only a theory that is well defended against recognition of the reality of this struggle – its reality today, for the vast majority of people alive now – could reinterpret this revolutionary optimism about the power of materialist pedagogy to disclose the inexhaustible as an outmoded fantasy about the masterful or Promethean human being standing astride nature and trying to dominate or colonize everything. The relation that Dietzgen and Marx tried to conceptualize – poetically, passionately and with philosophical daring, in the name of the proletariat and for individual workers – is not between a masterful human subject who knows everything and a nature that is there only to be dominated or colonized; the relation is between work and the inexhaustible. If mastery of a kind is nonetheless essential to the work that might be done to actualize this relation, it is because it is at the far reaches of discovery that work in this sense tends to get most seriously arduous, compelling, demanding and intense.

zh: 但如果说实际的对立性思维令新唯物主义者反感，某种对立的表示仍然被允许，只为维持体面。库尔和弗罗斯特在谈到他们的一些新唯物主义同行时写道：“一个马克思主义的标签，有助于表示他们对占主导地位的新自由主义趋势的反对。”导言的下一句话表明，他们说到“标签”时是认真的。他们写道：“在后结构主义及其批评之后，任何可行的马克思主义版本都不能推进一种历史元叙事，不能期望识别决定性的经济规律，不能推崇一种原初的、纯净的自然，也不能把共产主义设想为历史被理想化的物质命运。”
根据新唯物主义严苛的新标准，马克思本人的思想当然不够格成为马克思主义的“可行版本”。作为对照，《新唯物主义》文集中由 Pheng Cheah 和周蕾（Rey Chow）提供了“后结构主义及其批评”的一些可行版本。Cheah 解释说，马克思主义对“作为社会历史主体的无产阶级”的顽固依恋，使它无法认识到“与他异性的关系比作为实体或在场的物质更物质”。
因为马克思主义不能或不愿放弃阶级、历史和主体性，以及对立性思维的其他一切执念，它就被困在一个不够物质的物质概念中——这种物质比德里达的“没有唯物主义、甚至或许没有物质的物质性”更不物质。
这解释了马克思主义者为何未能领会：“不可能者奇怪地比具体实际更物质、更真实。”新唯物主义的物质比旧唯物主义的物质更物质；这种新的、更物质的物质性，在理论上让新唯物主义者的生活比马克思主义者更难，因为后者仍可天真地享受一种幻觉：经济规律可以被识别，共产主义可以被设想。新唯物主义者必须处理一种更物质的物质性，它不再“轻易由政治话语可识别的具体形象（例如工人阶级）所实例化”。
面对不可能者那更物质的物质性，像工人阶级这样易于实例化的具体形象并不可行。然而新唯物主义者不必绝望，因为究竟有什么具体形象可用来实例化物质性，毕竟甚至不是一个新问题；“也许更好的问题是”，Cheah 安慰地建议，“不要问这些新唯物主义与政治思想的相关性及其对具体政治的含义，而要问它们如何激进地置疑政治理论的基本范畴，包括政治本身的概念。”
en: But if actual oppositional thinking is antipathetic for new materialists, some signifying of opposition is nonetheless permissible, for the purposes of keeping up appearances. ‘A Marxist label’, write Coole and Frost of some of their fellow new materialists, ‘has helped to signify their opposition to dominant neoliberal trends.’ The next sentence of the introduction makes clear that when they say ‘label’, they mean it. ‘Coming after poststructuralism and its criticisms’, they write, ‘no workable version of Marxism can advance a historical metanarrative, aspire to the identification of determining economic laws, valorize an originary, pristine nature, or envisage communism as history’s idealized material destiny.’

Marx’s own thought would certainly not qualify as a ‘workable version’ of Marxism, according to the tough new stand ards of new materialism. For contrast, some workable versions of ‘poststructuralism and its criticisms’ are provided in the

volume by Pheng Cheah and Rey Chow. Cheah explains that Marxism’s stubborn attachment to the ‘proletariat as a sociohistorical subject’ stops it from recognizing that the ‘relation to alterity is more material than matter as substance or presence’.

Because Marxism cannot or will not let go of class, history and subjectivity, and all the other hang-ups of oppositional thought, it is stuck with a concept of matter that is not material enough, a matter that is less material than Derrida’s ‘materiality without materialism and even perhaps without matter.’

This explains the failure of Marxists to grasp that ‘the impossible is curiously more material and real than concrete actuality.’ The new materialist’s matter is more material than the old materialist’s matter, and this new, more material materiality makes life harder in theory for the new materialist than it was for the Marxist, who could still naively enjoy the delusion that economic laws can be identified and communism can be envisioned. The new materialist has to deal with a more material materiality that is no longer ‘easily instantiated by concrete figures that are recognizable by political discourse’, like the working class.

Easily instantiated concrete figures like the working class are not workable in light of the more material materiality of the impossible. Yet the new materialist need not despair, because the question what concrete figure might be available to instantiate materiality is after all not even a new question; ‘perhaps the better question to ask’, Cheah consolingly suggests, ‘is not that of the relevance of these new materialisms to political thought and their implications for concrete politics but how they radically put into question the fundamental categories of political theory including the concept of the political itself.’

zh: 新唯物主义者周蕾对“如何改变世界”这个旧而不可行的马克思主义问题另有更好的问题设想。她以一种自由主义的非排他精神——这种精神在此一直延伸到马克思主义废料场的边缘——问道：“如果我们采纳马克思主义对唯物主义/物质性的关注（作为批判意识哲学的一种方式），却不把它（像马克思主义往往那样）定义为一种带来改善性变革的能动力量，那会怎样？”
借用德里达的说法，简·贝内特对某一个马克思也同样好客。《德意志意识形态》《共产党宣言》和《资本论》的马克思或许不再可行，因为那个马克思是人道主义者；但在荣誉性的原初新唯物主义者名册中，可以为“写德谟克利特论文的马克思”留出位置——即为马克思按照大学提交规定、在身为大学成员并受学术知识礼仪规范约束时写下的那一篇作品留出位置。

与这部早期作品的精神及其对萌芽中的新唯物主义所作的充满希望的暗示相反，马克思不久便离开大学，成为一个好斗、大嗓门、狂放诗性的共产主义者；他对工人这一“社会历史主体”的前解构式执迷，使他犯了过高估计人类的错误。他最终成为贝内特所谓“物种自恋”的牺牲品——一种对我们之外事物的深度麻木，其养分是有毒信念：人类生命“特殊——也就是从根本上不同于物质”。认为我们活着并没有错；麻烦始于“我们人类……把自己看作［生命的］
特殊的表现形式”。
没有哪种聚苯乙烯、蝙蝠屎或系外行星会如此自恋，我们为何要如此？
难道人类独一无二地易受“人类中心偏见”影响吗？
（狄慈根显然从未成为这种自恋焦虑的猎物，尽管他是一个旧唯物主义者、一个人道主义者、一个未被解构的革命者：“人们对自己智力的骄傲是正当的，但把在他们看来头等重要的东西赋予世界之中的首要地位，则是幼稚的。”

）新唯物主义者罗西·布拉伊多蒂用一种令人安心地近似于新技术营销推介的语汇，庆祝后人类终于在新唯物主义中到来：它“经验上有根据，因为它被嵌入并被具身”，它“更像一个形象，而不像一个实体发挥作用”，它“是一种由理论驱动的制图工具，旨在充分理解……解构人类的过程”，它“提供了一个框架，以理解我们快速变化的时代中正在进行的成为主体的过程”，同时它“使我们能够跨越若干跨学科领域，追踪关于非人/非人性（inhuman）/跨人/元人/后人类的话语的出现，这些话语由对人本主义和人类中心主义的交叉批判所产生”。
但即便在这“新”之新曙光的光照下，人们仍发现有必要加一个清醒的警示。布拉伊多蒂说，所有这些收获都可能被“泛人类的重新发明”逆转；这种泛人类在天主教会的保守话语、企业泛人类主义和好战的军事干涉主义中“显而易见”，但更不祥的是，“它在进步左翼中更为迂回，却同样强大，那里社会主义人道主义的遗产提供了工具，把焦虑改造成政治狂怒”。
en: New Materialist Rey Chow has another idea for a better question than the old unworkable Marxist one about how to change the world. In a spirit of liberal non-exclusivity that here extends right up to the periphery of the Marxist scrapyard, she asks: ‘what if we were to adopt Marxism’s focus on materialism/ materiality (as a way to critique the philosophy of consciousness), yet without defining it (as Marxism tends to) as an agency of change-as-improvement?’
Jane Bennett is comparably hospitable to a certain Marx, to borrow Derrida’s phrase. The Marx of
and

may no longer be workable, since that Marx was a humanist, but room can be made in a roster of honorary proto-new materialists for ‘the Marx of his dissertation on Democritus’ – that is, for the one piece of writing that Marx did according to university regulations for submission, while he was a member of a university, constrained by the norms of academic intellectual decorum.

Contrary to the spirit of this early work and its promising intimations of the budding new materialism, Marx would shortly leave the university, and would become an aggressive, loud-mouthed, wildly poetic communist whose pre-deconstructive obsession with the ‘sociohistorical subject’ of the worker led him into the error of overvaluing human beings. He ended up a casualty of what Bennett calls ‘species-narcissism’, a kind of deep numbness to things other than ourselves, nourished by the toxic belief that human life is ‘special – that is, radically other to matter’. There is nothing wrong with thinking that we are alive; the trouble starts when ‘we humans … think of ourselves as the
special of [life’s] expressions’.
No polystyrene, bat shit or exoplanet would be so narcissistic, so why should we?
Can it be that humans are uniquely susceptible to ‘humancentric prejudice’?

(Dietzgen was apparently never prey to such anxieties about narcissism, despite being an old materialist, a humanist and an un-deconstructed revolutionary: ‘Men are, and have a right to be, proud of their intellect, but it is puerile to give to a thing, which appears to them of primary importance, the primacy of the world.’

) New materialist Rosi Braidotti, in an idiom reassuringly similar to that of a marketing pitch for a new technology, celebrates the arrival in new materialism of the posthuman that is at last ‘empirically grounded, because it is embedded and embodied’ and that ‘functions less as a substantive entity than a figuration’ and that ‘is a theoretically-powered cartographic tool that aims at achieving adequate understanding of … processes of undoing the human’ and that ‘provides a frame to understand the ongoing processes of becoming-subjects in our fast-changing times’, while it also ‘enables us to track, across a number of interdisciplinary fields, the emergence of discourses about the non/in/trans/meta/ post-human, which are generated by the intersecting critiques of humanism and of anthropocentrism’.

But even in this light of the new dawn of the new, one sober note of caution is found to be necessary. All these gains may yet be reversed, says Braidotti, by ‘the reinvention of a pan-human’, which is ‘explicit in the conservative discourse of the Catholic Church, in corporate pan-humanism, [and] belligerent military interventionism’, but which, more ominously, ‘is more oblique but equally strong in the progressive Left, where the legacy of socialist humanism provides the tools to re-work anxiety into political rage’.

zh: 新唯物主义者不去沉溺于用社会主义人道主义遗产的工具、由焦虑编造出来的政治狂怒，也不采用那种不符合“通过标签表示对主导结构之反对”要求的旧人道主义马克思主义；他们常常喜欢引用德勒兹。但他们拥抱的德勒兹，不是《反俄狄浦斯》中那个满口脏话、好斗的合著者；后者向学院提出的问题是：“人是否应当因为所吃之物而窒息，吞咽空气，用嘴拉屎？”

新唯物主义偏爱一套柔和的德勒兹母题调色板：晚期哲学写作中关于内在性、切口、褶皱、平面和生成的灰色与米色。德勒兹那野性的调色板，真正刺目的原色，那个充满他在尼采身上热爱并崇拜的攻击性与暴力的野兽派德勒兹，被礼貌的沉默略过。《反俄狄浦斯》的德勒兹是“主动的、攻击性的、艺术的、生产性的、凯旋的”德勒兹，是“狂野生产与爆炸性欲望”和“公开恶意的活动”的热爱者；他对“再现”逻辑的超暴力“精神分裂分析”攻击，如今几乎不合时宜得令人难以忍受（“整个欲望—
都被碾碎，屈从于
的要求，屈从于再现中代表者与被代表者的沉闷游戏”）。
这个特定的德勒兹痴迷于“性无处不在这一真相”，例如“资产阶级如何操无产阶级”，以及“希特勒如何让法西斯分子勃起”。
这个特定的德勒兹在新唯物主义手中遭受的，正是他在1965年论尼采的文章中所阐明的那种可鄙病态的命运：“他不再是诗人，而成为‘公共教授’”。
正如列宁在谈到“对对立性思维的厌恶”这一漫长历史中的另一段插曲时所说：“教授们利用并且想要利用大学的自由，不是为了煽起大火，而是为了扑灭它。”
en: Instead of wallowing in political rage fabricated out of anxiety using the tools of the legacy of socialist humanism, and instead of the old humanist Marxism that does not meet the requirements of signifying opposition to dominant structures by means of a label, new materialists often like to quote Deleuze. But the Deleuze they embrace is not the foul-mouthed, aggressive co-author of
, whose question for the academy was ‘Should one, or should one not, suffocate from what one eats, swallow air, shit with one’s mouth?’

New materialism prefers a muted palette of Deleuzean motifs, the greys and beiges of the late philosophical writing about immanence, cuts, folds, planes and becoming. The savage palette of Deleuze, the really lurid primary colours, the fauvist Deleuze full of the aggression and violence that he loved and idolized in Nietzsche, is passed over in polite silence. The Deleuze of

was the ‘active, aggressive, artistic, productive, and triumphant’ Deleuze, the lover of ‘wild production and explosive desire’ and of ‘openly malevolent activity’, the Deleuze whose ultra-violent, ‘schizoanalytic’ attack on the logic of ‘representation’ is now almost insufferably untimely (‘The whole of desiring-
is crushed, subjected to the requirements of
, and to the dreary games of what is representative and represented in representation’).
This certain Deleuze was obsessed with ‘the truth that sexuality is everywhere’, such as in ‘the way the bourgeoisie fucks the proletariat’ and in how ‘Hitler gave the fascists hard-ons’.

This certain Deleuze has suffered at the hands of new materialism the very fate whose despicable morbidity he spelled out in his 1965 essay on Nietzsche: ‘he ceases to be a poet and becomes a “public professor”’.

As Lenin said, with reference to another episode in the long history of ‘antipathy to oppositional ways of thinking’, ‘professors use and desire to use the freedom of the universities not to fan the conflagration but to extinguish it.’

zh: 这一切都回到诗学，最终回到马克思《资本论》的诗学。布拉伊多蒂称为“解构人类”、贝内特称为克服我们的“物种自恋”的理论化，从根本上是在禁止那种真正暴烈而革命的自我灭绝的诗学。新唯物主义宣告放弃宏大的自我、膨胀的自我、跨立世界的自我、与动物和物质不同且更优越的自我，但实际上，它靠一种通过滴灌大量施予的否定配方，让所有这些令人反感的角色保持活着。真正被从新唯物主义的万有理论中排除掉的自我，不是自大狂或夸张化的自我，而是被压碎、被掏空、被无限削小的自我：马克思的工人——其在资本关系中的存在，是无关紧要的暴风雪中的“尘埃性”。

通过把一种内在于物质本身的新的“平等主义”理论化，通过推出新的物质概念，使它包摄生命、宇宙以及一切可能被评价之物，通过坚持这种物质性是一种比任何对立性思维（或革命社会批判）所梦见过的都更物质的物质性，新唯物主义实际上糊住了社会现实中那道无底裂缝——在那里，尚待物质化的存在之尘埃卡在永恒的坠落中。说明这一意味的一种方式是：新唯物主义漫不经心地废除了马克思从亚里士多德那里发展出的潜能逻辑——正是这种逻辑塑造了工人的形象：他还远不能过上我们知道应当属于我们的生活；这个活着的个体被世界阻挡、压碎、掏空，正因如此，他很久以前就等同于任何物质事物，甚至早于新平等主义的福音，因为人类与聚苯乙烯在‘从价值对象性来看’完全无关紧要这一点上完全一样。
en: All this comes back to poetics, and ultimately back to the poetics of Marx’s

. The theorizing that Braidotti calls ‘undoing the human’ and Bennett calls getting over our ‘species- narcissism’ is fundamentally about proscribing the really violent and revolutionary poetics of self-extinction. New materialism proclaims its renunciation of the grandiose self, the inflated ego, the self astride the world, the self that is different from and better than animals and matter, but in fact it keeps all these objectionable personae alive on a formula of repudiation liberally administered by drip-feed. The self that is actually written out of new materialism’s theory of everything is not the egomaniacal or hyperbolized self but the one that is crushed, emptied and infinitely diminished: Marx’s worker, whose existence in the capital-relation is ‘specklikeness’ in a blizzard of indifference.

By theorizing a new ‘egalitarianism’ intrinsic in matter itself, by rolling out the new concept of matter so that it comprehends life, the universe and everything that could ever be valued, and by insisting that this materiality is a more material materiality than any oppositional mode of thinking (or revolutionary social criticism) ever dreamt of, new materialism in effect papers over the bottomless crack in social reality where the speck of existence that is yet to be materialized is stuck in a perpetual plummet. One way of saying what this means is to say that new materialism casually abolishes the logic of potentiality that Marx developed out of Aristotle to create the figure of the worker who is not yet anywhere near being able to live the life that we know is meant for us; the living individual who is blocked, crushed and emptied by the world and who precisely for that reason was long ago equal to any and every material thing, even prior to the good news about the new egalitarianism, since the human being and polystyrene are perfectly alike in being ‘value-objectively’ a matter of complete indifference.

zh: 另一种说法是：新唯物主义特地抽空了那种攻击性，而它作为社会革命思想形式的唯物主义批判史一直不可或缺。马克思的写作充满暴烈的批判：这种暴力不只是谴责或模仿，而是反击并引爆社会关系的暴力，它以概念和想象的极端去考验那些社会关系逻辑在诗性火焰的错乱之下还能支撑多久。马克思的唯物主义批判不是像教科书那样推进，而是旋转进入伪科学的、或认知上难以处理的概念化谵妄，把可感觉者与超感觉者、物理学与经济学、李嘉图与狼人、蝙蝠屎与黑格尔强行拼在一起，抓取政治经济学的语言，拉出其骇人地凸出的反讽内脏，处处违反其自身范畴逻辑的词汇纪律。所有这些都是马克思的

：马克思思想的唯物主义就在那里，不在那些关于所谓目的论的、熟悉而其实懒惰且虚构的投射中，也不在那种被动惰性的物质世界、以及跨立其上挥舞辩证法的伟大普罗米修斯式人类的图景中（那只是教授们的自由主义宣传），而在对工人已灭绝的自我与生命的逻辑上操蛋的、幻想的、不可忍受地真实的描述中：一个原子尘埃，在价值增殖无限性的螺旋下被碾碎。马克思对人类生命的唯物主义愿景，对主体施加巨大压力，迫使其经验这一真理；正如体力劳动者、旧唯物主义者狄慈根曾写道的，这意味着像脑中烈火一样感受它。
en: Another way of saying the same thing is that new materialism specifically evacuates the aggression that has been essential to the history of materialist criticism as a form of socially revolutionary thought. Marx’s writing is full of violent critique: a violence that does not merely condemn, or mimic, but that reacts against and sparks off the violence of social relations, by testing to conceptual and imaginative extremes the strength of the logic of those social relations to hold up under the derangements of poetic fire. Marx’s materialist critique proceeds not like a textbook but by spinning out into deliriums of pseudoscientific or cognitively intractable conceptualization, jamming together the sensuous and supersensuous, physics and economics, Ricardo and the werewolf, bat shit and Hegel, grabbing at the language of political economy and pulling out its gruesomely obtruding ironic innards, violating at every turn the lexical discipline of its own logic of categories. All this is Marx’s

: the materialism of Marx’s thought is right there, not in the familiar, and in fact lazy and fictitious, projections about so-called teleology, or the passive and inert world of matter astride which stands the great Promethean human being swinging his dialectics, which is just the liberal propaganda of professors, but in the logically fucked-up, fantastical, intolerably true description of the extinct self and life of the worker as an atomic speck crushed under the spiral of valorization’s infinity. Marx’s materialist vision of human life puts intense pressure on the subject to experience this truth, which means, as the manual labourer and old materialist Dietzgen once wrote, to feel it like a fire in the brain.

, Cambridge: Polity Press, 2018, p. 58. My criticism is related to this one but is different.
